name: Hardingfele slått (Hardanger-fiddle dance-tunes)
lineage: Norwegian Hardanger-fiddle slått dance-tune tradition of western-Norwegian mountain valleys (Hardanger, Voss, Telemark, Setesdal, Numedal regions). The hardingfele Hardanger-fiddle has four bowed melody strings plus four-or-five sympathetic resonant strings beneath the fingerboard, producing characteristic shimmering-overtone resonance. Slått (singular slått, plural slåttar) are solo virtuoso dance-tunes with strict regional-stylistic-conventions: springar three-beat asymmetric dance-tune, gangar two-beat walking-dance, halling acrobatic-male-display-dance, and rull rolling-tune. Performance: solo Hardanger-fiddle, with each regional sub-tradition (Setesdal, Hallingdal, Numedal, Valdres, Telemark) maintaining distinctive playing-conventions and ornamental-vocabulary.
